berlin.notes: Mapped perimeter blocks and courtyards give a coherent urban scene at the target detail. Individual roof materials, courtyard vegetation and fittings are inferred; exact building appearance remains unverified.

haworth.notes: The village road/building layout generates, but large surrounding areas become generic paving and roofs lack local variety. Initial spawn was obstructed; a shared clearance rule now gives a driveable start without changing the bake.

granada.notes: The Mediterranean fallback produces a distinct tiled-roof old town with mapped narrow streets. Roof colour is overly uniform, some roof/courtyard edges need stronger geometry checks, and the hilly setting is flattened.

industrial.notes: Large warehouses receive a different roof treatment and the water boundary is present. Yard surfaces and water are visibly plain; loading equipment, quay detail and street furniture are missing. This is not sufficient harbour realism.

forest.notes: Zero generated trees: the current vector-land-use path produced no forest mask, so the forest became open grass. A separate diagnostic detects tree cover across about 70 percent of this exact sample using the existing land-cover adapter. That layer was not added to this frozen experiment.

dry.notes: Dry ground and a narrow road generate without invented urban pavements. Large repeated flat ground, missing scrub and absent terrain relief prevent accurate reproduction of the badlands.
